title: Jennifer Lopez Talks Viral 'Six Fingers Left' Moment, Life After Divorce
summary: Jennifer Lopez talked a fan's viral reaction to her recent divorce comments and shared how she channeled heartbreak into lessons on SiriusXM.
body_markdown:
[Jennifer Lopez](https://www.siriusxm.com/blog/tag/jennifer-lopez) is still thinking about a fan interaction that left her in stitches.


The “On the Floor” singer joined the hosts of[SiriusXM Hits 1](https://www.siriusxm.com/blog/tag/siriusxm-hits-1) The Morning Mash up for a Front Row in the New York City studio, November 17, and spoked about the viral moment where a fan reacted to her comments about being married four times. Listen to the full interview on the[SiriusXM app](https://sxm.app.link/BlogJenniferLopezFrontRow) .


[Jennifer Lopez Front Row SiriusXM Hits 1 Listen on the App Listen on the App](https://sxm.app.link/BlogJenniferLopezFrontRow)


“That was the funniest thing I’ve ever heard in my life, it made me laugh out loud. I had to get up. I almost fell. It was just hysterical,” Jennifer told Nicole Ryan and Ryan Sampson. “Rachel Zegler, who I love and who is an angel, she was asking me something, and she didn’t ask me anything that was weird or inappropriate or anything, but I brought up being married or something and I put up my fingers like, ‘four times,’ and somebody goes, ‘You still got six fingers left.'”


For Jennifer, learning from the heartbreak is the biggest medicine when it comes to healing.


“It was like learning the same thing over and over. It took me a minute to get it and it’s fine,” she shared. “It’s fine because I think that there was love that was involved and there was heartache and there was lessons. You really realized, it doesn’t matter what people do to you or any of that. What matters is what you’re doing in it or how you got there and figuring out yourself. It was really about figuring out myself every single time.”


Jennifer—who ended her second marriage to Ben Affleck in 2025—also added that the end of her relationship allowed her to feel life’s growing pains.


“For me, and having recently gone through one a couple years ago, it really felt like it was such a like growth spurt for me,” she said. “I just delved into, ‘You know what? I have to figure out what I’m doing here.’ I felt like I did when the kids were born, but there’s another few pieces that I’m not getting. I just haven’t got it yet, it’s okay it’s a long life.”


Part of living that life is fully embracing who she is.


“I had a therapist who told me, ‘You’re looking at it, some people never even look, so people never figure it out.’ He’s like, ‘You’re so young, keep going and keep discovering yourself and learn to love every part of yourself in that way. Even the parts that are the hopeless romantic and all of that that.”


Looking at the end of a love has offered a new perspective and energy to channel into performing. Which is what she did with her Up All Night Las Vegas residency, the concert highlighted in her upcoming film, *The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas* .


“That’s the artist in me,” JLo said. “That’s the dreamer in me. That’s the person who creates the things that I get to create. That’s the brave person who gets out in front of 50,000 people and dances around and does flips live on air. You have to be a little bit crazy.”
